newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian parliamentarians question Di Rupo charges.
newsitem.headline: Belgian parliamentarians question Di Rupo charges.

text.p: Two members of the special Belgian parliamentary commission studying anonymous allegations that Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo had sex with under-age boys on Tuesday questioned the quality of the case against him.

"The second file is very different from the first case. It consists of various items of dubious value," Francophone Socialist member of parliament Serge Moureaux told Reuters just before the commission was due to hear evidence from fellow Francophone Socialist Di Rupo.

The Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, said on Monday that the allegations in the first file against Di Rupo, based on a statement from a sole witness, were baseless. However, it asked the commission to study the second file.
"The second file is even lighter than the first," Flemish Socialist member of the commission Renaat Landruyt told Reuters.

He said the file consisted of transcripts of anonymous telephone calls and anonymous letters, the validity of which was even harder to check than the statements made by witness Oliver Trugsnach in the first case file.
Di Rupo, a homosexual, has always denied being involved in paedophilia.
